Collapse coordinates that repeat

Source: R/grid.R
collapse_duplicates.Rd

Triangulation has nothing to say about two values at the same place, and Qhull refuses outright. Real data does this constantly: a station occupied twice, a transect that crosses its own track, coordinates rounded to a printed precision.

Usage

collapse_duplicates(
  xy,
  value,
  fun = mean,
  quiet = FALSE,
  fun_label = deparse(substitute(fun))
)

Arguments

xy

coordinates, two columns

value

one value per row of xy

fun

function used to combine the values at a repeated coordinate

quiet

do not report how many coordinates were collapsed

fun_label

name of fun to use in that report

Value

A list of xy and value, with no repeated coordinate.

Details

So decide explicitly. collapse_duplicates() reduces repeated coordinates to one, combining their values with fun, and says how many it collapsed.

Examples

xy <- cbind(c(1, 2, 2, 3), c(1, 2, 2, 3))
collapse_duplicates(xy, c(10, 20, 30, 40))
#> 1 duplicated coordinate collapsed with mean()
#> $xy
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    1
#> [2,]    2    2
#> [3,]    3    3
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 10 25 40
#>
